question.value: Is formamide (NH2CHO) chemically related to HNCO and/or H2CO, as tested by comparing moment maps and LTE-modelled abundances in three high-mass star-forming regions?

evidence.quote: We aim to find empirical evidence to support the chemical relationships of formamide to HNCO and H$_2$CO.
The sources were observed with ALMA in Cycle 2 in July and September 2015 (2013.1.00489.S) in Band 6

analysis_steps.goal: Extract spectra and model with LTE

method.value: Extract spectra at NH2CHO peak pixels from continuum-subtracted images; fit NH2CHO, HNCO, H2CO and potential blenders (C2H5OH, CH3CN v8=1, CH3(18)OH) simultaneously in XCLASS

evidence.quote: performing simultaneous fits of the species NH$_2$CHO, HNCO, H$_2$CO, and species that were potentially blended with NH$_2$CHO

key_parameters.value: Tex 50-300 K for HNCO and NH2CHO, 70-400 K for H2CO; FWHM and vLSR constrained by Gaussian fits, vLSR free within ±0.5 km/s

evidence.quote: The $T_\mathrm{ex}$ free parameter was allowed to vary between 50 and 300 K for HNCO and NH$_2$CHO and between 70 and 400 K for H$_2$CO.

assumptions.value: LTE; H2CO modeled with source size ~0.15'' below beam

evidence.quote: The temperature of H$_2$CO was modeled using higher temperatures and a source size smaller than the beam size ($\sim0.15''$)

assumptions.value: N(H2) from continuum with Tdust=100 K, kappa=1.0 cm2/g, gas-to-dust 100

evidence.quote: assuming a T$_{dust}$ of 100 K, a dust opacity of 1.0 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: Ossenkopf1994), and a gas-to-dust ratio of 100
The errors shown were determined using the *errorestim$\_$ins* algorithm using the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method built into the XCLASS software.

validation.value: Blending checked with ethanol comparison line at 217803.69 MHz

evidence.quote: the peak integrated emission of NH$_2$CHO (1) is $\sim$8 times stronger than that of C$_2$H$_5$OH

analysis_steps.goal: Compare moment-0 peak positions and extent

method.value: Locate emission peaks with 2D Gaussian fits and measure peak separations between NH2CHO and HNCO/H2CO

evidence.quote: we locate the peak of line emission to high accuracy with a 2D-Gaussian fit accuracy to 0.01$''$

assumptions.value: Species with same peak, velocity and line width are in the same gas and related

evidence.quote: if two species peak in the same location, and have the same velocity and line width, then they are in the same gas

validation.value: RADEX optical depths estimated: H2CO 33-430, HNCO 0.4-69

evidence.quote: the optical depths for the H$_2$CO lines range from 33-430 while those for HNCO lines are much lower ranging from 0.4-69

method.value: Subtract moment-1 and moment-2 maps between species; histogram absolute differences and use mean and standard deviation; same-species transition pairs give an internal error

evidence.quote: The average value and standard deviation of these histograms were used to determine which species was most similar to NH$_2$CHO.

validation.value: Internal error from two transitions of the same species

evidence.quote: two transitions from the same species were also compared to determine the "internal error"

method.value: Divide modeled Ncol by core N(H2); fit power laws between species pairs

evidence.quote: Modeled $N_\mathrm{col}$ values were divided by the H$_2$ column densities listed in Table [2](#spectrapoints) to obtain abundances for comparison
The fit for NH$_2$CHO vs. HNCO is \[*X*(NH$_2$CHO)=0.06 *X*(HNCO)$^{0.95}$\] (R$^2$=0.93).

findings_qualitative.value: HNCO emission peaks are closer to NH2CHO than H2CO peaks, and H2CO is much more extended

evidence.quote: it is clear that the integrated emission peaks of HNCO are closer to the peaks of NH$_2$CHO than the H$_2$CO peaks.

claims.hypothesis: NH2CHO is spatially and kinematically more related to HNCO than to H2CO
claims.experiment: Moment-0, 1 and 2 map comparisons in six subsources
claims.result: Peaks and dispersions mostly favor HNCO; velocity fields split equally
claims.finding: HNCO has a slightly stronger relationship with NH2CHO

evidence.quote: From these overall results, it seems that HNCO has a slightly stronger relationship with NH$_2$CHO.

claims.hypothesis: Abundances of NH2CHO correlate with HNCO and H2CO
claims.experiment: XCLASS LTE abundances and power-law fits
claims.result: All pairs R^2>0.93; HNCO relation matches Lopez-Sepulcre et al. 2015
claims.finding: Abundance correlation is not a good indicator of direct chemical relationship

evidence.quote: The correlation between abundances of all three pairs of species suggests that such a correlation is not a good indicator of a direct chemical relationship.

limitations_admitted.value: H2CO opacity may cause the differences in distribution and kinematics

evidence.quote: It is possible that the greater differences in spatial distribution, velocity, and dispersion between H$_2$CO and NH$_2$CHO compared to HNCO arise from optical depth issues.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 2-3 transitions per species; LTE single-pixel fits with H2CO optically thick
Only six subsources, so abundance correlations are not independent tests
Similarity metric lacks formal significance threshold
